episodes.159532: Offshore moving thunderstorms produced a couple of strong wind gusts along the Brevard County coast.
episodes.159608: A weak disturbance crossed through West Virginia on the evening of August 3rd which prompted scattered showers and thunderstorms across the region. One storm in particular resulted in downed trees in the town of Mount Clare and minor flooding in Shinnston.
episodes.160271: On the afternoon of August 4, 2021, a marginally severe thunderstorm moved over the City of Great Falls, MT, which produced hail as it moved from west to east across the city. Most of the reports that were received were around 3/4, but there were two separate reports of 1 hail in the city.
episodes.160302: Eureka Airport measured severe winds from a thunderstorm in the area.
episodes.160823: A thunderstorm strengthened as it moved south across eastern Natrona County. The storm became severe as it approached Casper, producing quarter-sized hail in and around Evansville.
episodes.160916: A line of high-based thunderstorms produced some wind gusts over 60 mph over portions of Fall River County.
episodes.161120: A weak front was stalled near the I-10 corridor, and a weak surface low developed on the boundary in the NE Gulf of Mexico. Small waves of mid level energy rotated around the east side of the low across the local area and combined with precipitable water of well over 2 inches, locally heavy rainfall developed with localized flooding across the Suwannee River Valley.
episodes.161284: An isolated thunderstorm produced some severe wind gusts around Park County.
episodes.161689: Isolated cluster of severe storms developed along the South Dakota/Nebraska border and moved southeast across portions of north central Nebraska.
episodes.161920: Widespread severe weather occurred in southeast Idaho.
episodes.162410: A persistent rainy pattern across the southeastern big bend brought rainfall amounts in excess of foot during the first 12 days of the month to portions of southeastern Taylor, southern Lafayette, and Dixie counties. This rainfall fell on already saturated grounds and resulted in significant, long duration areal flooding. In addition, significant river flooding occurred across the Steinhatchee River basin. The Steinhatchee River crested at its 2nd highest crest on record at 24.6 ft on August 7th, which is well into the moderate flood category. Many roads were closed, and many homes were impacted. The river remained in at least minor flood stage for 20 days.
episodes.162620: Despite weaker pre-storm deep-layer shear on the order of 25-30 knots and fairly narrow instability profiles of 1000-1500 J/kg, modifications on the storm scale and an increase in the low-level jet improved the environment enough to support several long-lived supercell clusters along a weak frontal boundary.
episodes.162796: Strong daytime heating from a building ridge and rotating disturbances around the ridge brought moisture with isolated thunderstorms into southeastern Oregon and southeastern Idaho.
